Text is Steve's take, written with him (approved direction Nov 17, 2026: confident tone; Demin 'watching closer'; Traoré speed/downhill, efficiency, beating slot; Stirtz connector IQ, OKC development, followed him at Drake and Iowa).

groups.title: Brooklyn's backcourt
groups.take: Brooklyn hit on both of its 2025 guards, and I want them together. Traoré is the engine. He lives going downhill, and it's turning into real production: 13.6 a night on 61% true shooting in 23 minutes. He went 19th and he's producing like a top-7 pick in his class. Demin is the one I'm watching closer. The model has him as a Volume Shooter, the type it trusts least, because his BYU season was heavy on usage and turnovers. But a 6'9" guard who averaged almost 8 assists per 40 doesn't come around often, and he's started every game he's played. If his shot holds up, Brooklyn has its backcourt.

groups.title: Bennett Stirtz
groups.take: I've been on Stirtz since Drake. I watched him run Ben McCollum's offense there, followed him to Iowa when McCollum moved, and saw him put up 19.8 a game against Big Ten defenses without forcing anything. The model agrees with me: he's a Connector, the archetype that has beaten its draft slot. Now he's in OKC, the best place in the league for a guy like this to develop, and he's already earning 18 minutes a night as a rookie on a deep roster. He's producing ahead of where he went at 16, and the minutes are only going up from here.
